newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada agency delays V-chip violence ratings date.
newsitem.headline: Canada agency delays V-chip violence ratings date.

text.p: The Canadian Radio-Television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) on Friday delayed by a year the deadline for broadcasters to start a rating system aimed at excessive television violence after it became clear that the previously set September deadline could not be met.
"A number of issues must still be resolved before the system can be made widely available," CRTC chairwoman Francoise Bertrand said in a press release.
She said the CRTC decision was prompted by a request from the Action Group on Violence on Television for more time to prepare a user-friendly system.

"Although we wanted to see it introduced in September 1996, AGVOT has indicated that it needs extra time to develop the best possible and most user-friendly system that is needed to offer consumers a perfectly reliable, long-term parental control tool," Bertrand said.

Under the new system, Canadian programmers will be responsible for encoding the programs they broadcast to activate a special device called the V-chip. The V-chip could be pre-set to block out programs parents consider too violent for their children to watch.

"Canadian programming services are to begin classifying and encoding their programming for the beginning of the new fall season in 1997," the CRTC said. "The Commission strongly expects broadcast distributors to make V-chip-equipped set-top boxes available to Canadian consumers by the fall of 1997."
September 1997 will also be the new deadline for Canadian TV distributors, including cable companies, to ensure that foreign signals they distribute are also encoded, the CRTC said.
About 70 percent of Canada's TV programming consists of U.S. shows and Canada has been working closely with the United States which has mandated its own version of the V-chip for new U.S. TV sets.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
